- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.28), model often overshoots upward; cap upward revisions or adjust downward early.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overcorrects with a steep downward forecast; smooth out the dip.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 days of declining prices), model often fails to recognize it; forecast should align with recent trend direction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early days (1-5) when sentiment is neutral or positive; reduce initial forecast values.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model often underestimates; add small upward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently underestimates when true price rises sharply after a low; adjust for momentum in low-to-high transitions.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.06–0.17), model often overfits to recent highs; use moving average or weighted average to dampen noise.
